# lab-proxy

HAProxy, routing the lab's hostnames to the cluster that claimed them.

<!-- Generated by nix build .#referencePages -->

## Inputs

| input | type | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| httpPort | null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive) | `the lab's slot in `lib/allocation.nix`` | Loopback port the HTTP listener is published on.  Null takes the lab's allocated slot, which is every lab in this tree. Set it to move off one: an allocated port looks free in a table of registered names and may not be — the ranges contain 5353 (mDNS) and 5355 (LLMNR), and a host already running something is a fact no allocation can see.  |
| httpsPort | null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive) | `the lab's slot in `lib/allocation.nix`` | Loopback port the HTTPS listener is published on.  Null takes the lab's allocated slot, which is every lab in this tree. Set it to move off one: an allocated port looks free in a table of registered names and may not be — the ranges contain 5353 (mDNS) and 5355 (LLMNR), and a host already running something is a fact no allocation can see.  |
| idleTimeout | string | `"1h"` | How long an idle connection is held open.  Long, deliberately. HAProxy's defaults are tens of seconds, which orderly-closes the long-lived streams that gRPC and watch-based clients keep open — and the symptom is not a failure but a client that silently reconnects forever.  |
| image | string | `"haproxy:3.1-alpine"` | HAProxy container image. |

## What it emits

Rendered by `homelab.dns` as the lab unit `proxy`. A unit of the lab
installs nothing into a cluster, and its provisions are sealed inside the
lab's inclusion — so its declaration above is its interface.
